Oh, thank you, Rocio. My hands were cold from the shock!
And look: this soft wool cardigan is clean and unworn. Try it on.
Are you sure? It looks lovely and nice and warm!
It fits you very well, madam.
You good people are saving my whole trip.
A traveller cannot sit sad on her first evening in Valencia!
I locked the other blue suitcase safely in our closet.
Thank you, Mateo. That little wooden train looked old and cherished.
Its owner will surely look for it very soon.
I think I am going to sleep well tonight after all.
Rest well, madam. Ring the bell if you need anything.

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: Polite form of address: señora Carmen.

examples.trans: The madam is here.

examples.text: Vemos las señoras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the madams from the door.

meanings.note: Accented té ('tea') distinguishes the noun from pronoun te ('you').

examples.trans: The tea is here.

examples.text: Vemos los tés desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the teas from the door.

meanings.note: Describes hot drinks, food, or water.

examples.trans: It is a hot piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene, señora: té caliente de menta con miel.
examples.trans: Here you are, madam: hot mint tea with honey.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Té de menta = mint tea.

examples.text: La menta es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The mint is very important here.
We talk about the mint.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.
Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la miel.

examples.text: La miel es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The honey is very important here.
We talk about the honey.

meanings.note: Expresses surprise, sympathy, or mild dismay.

examples.trans: Oh, I nearly forgot my umbrella!
Goodness, what a fright you gave me!

meanings.note: Gracias por + noun/infinitive expresses 'thank you for...'.

examples.trans: Thank you very much for your help!
Thank you for coming today.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.trans: The windows face the garden.
We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Feminine despite ending in -o: la mano, las manos; a mano derecha = on your right-hand side.

examples.text: Gira después de la farmacia a mano derecha.
examples.trans: Turn past the pharmacy on your right-hand side.
My hands are clean.

meanings.note: As a masculine noun (el frío), means 'the cold'.

examples.trans: It is a cold piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene un paño limpio y agua fría, Ernesto.
examples.trans: Here is a clean cloth and cold water, Ernesto.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.
I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: ¡Qué susto! = What a fright!

examples.trans: The fright is here.

examples.text: Vemos los sustos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the frights from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.
This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: Light jacket or knitted cardigan.

examples.trans: The jacket is here.

examples.text: Vemos las chaquetas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the jackets from the door.

meanings.note: De lana = woollen.

examples.text: La lana es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The wool is very important here.
We talk about the wool.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.trans: It is a soft piece.

examples.text: Y mire: esta chaqueta de lana suave está limpia y nueva. Pruébela.
examples.trans: And look: this soft wool cardigan is clean and unworn. Try it on.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.
Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Opposite of sucio (dirty).

examples.trans: It is a clean piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene un paño limpio y agua fría, Ernesto.
examples.trans: Here is a clean cloth and cold water, Ernesto.

meanings.note: De nuevo is an idiom meaning 'again'.

examples.trans: It is a new piece.

examples.text: ¡Ah, se abre! Gracias. Soy Clara, la nueva recepcionista.
examples.trans: Oh, it opens! Thank you. I am Clara, the new receptionist.

probar.gloss: to try; to taste; to test

meanings.en: to try; to taste; to test
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: pruebo).

examples.text: Prueba este pan con aceite de oliva.
examples.trans: Try this bread with olive oil.

examples.text: Ayer probamos la mermelada de manzana.
examples.trans: Yesterday we tasted the apple jam.

meanings.note: Seguro que... = I bet / probably...

examples.trans: It is a sure piece.
Are you sure? It looks lovely and nice and warm!

meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg parezco.

examples.text: Este rincón parece un jardín secreto.
examples.trans: This corner looks like a secret garden.
The idea seemed excellent to us.

meanings.note: Warm everyday compliment in Spain (qué patio tan precioso).

examples.trans: It is a lovely piece.
Are you sure? It looks lovely and nice and warm!

meanings.note: Shortened form of mucho used before adjectives and adverbs.

examples.trans: The sponge cake is very tasty.

examples.text: Camina muy rápido por el puente.
examples.trans: She walks very fast across the bridge.

meanings.note: Affectionate diminutive of caliente.

examples.trans: It is a nice and warm piece.
Are you sure? It looks lovely and nice and warm!

meanings.note: Third-person singular indirect object pronoun.

examples.text: Le llevo una taza de té caliente.
examples.trans: I am bringing you/her a cup of hot tea.
Do you like the courtyard room?

quedar.gloss: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)

meanings.en: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)
meanings.note: Versatile verb: quedan dos ('two left'), le queda bien ('suits you'), quedar al mediodía ('meet at noon'), quedarse ('stay').

examples.trans: Only two vacant rooms are left.

examples.text: Esa chaqueta te queda muy bien.
examples.trans: That jacket suits you very well.

meanings.note: Before an adjective (bien caliente), means 'nice and hot'.

examples.trans: Everything is going very well today.
The tea comes out nice and hot.

meanings.note: Takes 3rd-person plural verbs (pasen ustedes).

examples.trans: Do you all have a reservation?

examples.text: El patio es para todos ustedes.
examples.trans: The courtyard is for all of you.

meanings.note: First-person singular object/reflexive pronoun.

examples.trans: Can you pass me the salt, please?
I live here and I work here.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Un paraguas a tiempo salva el paseo.
examples.trans: A timely umbrella saves the walk.

examples.text: Tu idea rápida salvó todo el desayuno.
examples.trans: Your quick idea saved the whole breakfast.

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Guía de viajes = travel guide.

examples.trans: The trip is here.

examples.text: Vemos los viajes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the trips from the door.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Masculine: el viajero.

examples.trans: The traveller is here.

examples.text: Vemos las viajeras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the travellers from the door.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

poder.gloss: can; to be able to; may

meanings.en: can; to be able to; may
meanings.note: Irregular: puedo, pude, podría.

examples.trans: May I look at the tag again?

examples.text: Hoy podemos desayunar en el patio.
examples.trans: Today we can have breakfast in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Estar triste = to feel sad.

examples.trans: It is a sad piece.

examples.text: ¡Una viajera no puede estar triste su primera tarde en Valencia!
examples.trans: A traveller cannot sit sad on her first evening in Valencia!

su.gloss: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)

meanings.en: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)
meanings.note: Plural sus (su maleta / sus maletas).

examples.trans: Here is your key, madam.

examples.text: Sus habitaciones están en la primera planta.
examples.trans: Your rooms are on the first floor.

meanings.note: Shortens to primer before masculine singular nouns (el primer día); also used as adverb ('first').

examples.text: Hoy es mi primer día de trabajo.
examples.trans: Today is my first day of work.
The first room is vacant.

meanings.note: Por la tarde = in the afternoon; ¡Buenas tardes! = Good afternoon!; llegar tarde = arrive late.

examples.trans: Good afternoon! Do you have a room free?

examples.text: Perdón por llegar un poco tarde.
examples.trans: Sorry for arriving a little late.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.
We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: Past-participle adjective from guardar.

examples.trans: It is a kept safe piece.

examples.text: De momento, su maleta sigue guardada bajo llave.
examples.trans: For now, his suitcase stays safe under lock and key.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Spanish never puts un/una before otro (otra taza = another cup; otra vez = again).

examples.trans: Would you like another cup of coffee?

examples.text: Míralo otra vez a la luz.
examples.trans: Look at it again in the light.

meanings.note: Hacer la maleta = to pack one's suitcase.

examples.trans: This blue suitcase is very heavy.

examples.text: Guardo las llaves en la maleta.
examples.trans: I keep the keys in the suitcase.

meanings.note: Plural azules; azul marino means 'navy blue'.

examples.trans: It is a blue piece.

examples.text: Espere, ¡es azul oscuro, igual que la suya!
examples.trans: Wait, it is dark blue, just like yours!

meanings.note: Versatile everyday noun for door keys, shut-off valves, and spanners.

examples.trans: The key is here.

examples.text: Vemos las llaves desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the keys from the door.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.
Our neighbours have coffee here.

meanings.note: Tall storage closet or bedroom wardrobe.

examples.trans: The wardrobe is here.

examples.text: Vemos los armarios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the wardrobes from the door.

meanings.note: Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas.

examples.trans: Pass me that blue notebook.

examples.text: Esa maleta pertenece a un cliente.
examples.trans: That suitcase belongs to a guest.

meanings.note: Diminutive of el tren.

examples.trans: The little train is here.

examples.text: Vemos los trenecitos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the little trains from the door.

meanings.note: De madera = wooden.

examples.trans: The wood is here.

examples.text: Vemos las maderas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the woods from the door.

meanings.note: Placed after a noun, means 'historic' or 'old-fashioned'.

examples.trans: It is an old piece.

examples.text: Encantada, Tomás, ¡siempre que nadie hable de vender pianos antiguos!
examples.trans: Gladly, Tomas, as long as nobody talks about selling old pianos!

meanings.note: Also used as an affectionate noun (queridos míos = my dears).

examples.trans: It is a dear piece.

examples.text: La vida organiza mejores dúos que nosotros, queridos míos.
examples.trans: Life arranges better duets than we do, my dear boys.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

meanings.note: Feminine: la dueña.

examples.trans: The owner is here.

examples.text: Vemos los dueños desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the owners from the door.

buscar.gloss: to look for; to search for

meanings.en: to look for; to search for
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'for' (busco la llave = I am looking for the key).

examples.trans: I am looking for the blue door.

examples.text: Ayer busqué mis gafas por toda la casa.
examples.trans: Yesterday I looked for my glasses all over the house.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta pronto! = See you soon!

examples.trans: See you soon and safe travels!

examples.text: Esta mañana me desperté muy pronto.
examples.trans: This morning I woke up very early.

meanings.note: Preterite 3rd sg/pl spells y: creyó, creyeron.

examples.text: Creo que el tren llega a tiempo.
examples.trans: I think the train is arriving on time.

examples.text: No podía creer tanta buena suerte.
examples.trans: He could not believe such good luck.

meanings.note: ¡Buenas noches! = Good evening / Good night; esta noche = tonight.

examples.trans: The night is here.

examples.text: Vemos las noches desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the nights from the door.

meanings.note: Ir a + infinitive expresses near future ('going to do').

examples.text: Voy a abrir la puerta ahora.
examples.trans: I am going to open the door now.
How is everything going this morning?

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue in present: duermo; o -> u in preterite 3rd: durmió).

examples.trans: I sleep eight hours every night.
Last night I slept wonderfully here.

meanings.note: Después de + noun/infinitive means 'after'.

examples.trans: We will talk after breakfast.
What do we do after that?

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Descanso media hora después de comer.
examples.trans: I rest half an hour after lunch.
The guests rested very well.

meanings.note: Dos toques cortos = two short rings.

examples.trans: The ring is here.

examples.text: Vemos los toques desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rings from the door.

meanings.note: Tocar el timbre = ring the bell.

examples.trans: The bell is here.

examples.text: Vemos los timbres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bells from the door.

meanings.note: Unaccented conjunction, distinct from accented sí ('yes').

examples.trans: Let me know if you need another blanket.

examples.text: Mira si queda leche en la nevera.
examples.trans: Check whether any milk is left in the fridge.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.trans: I need a pen to sign.
Do you all need another towel?

meanings.note: Indefinite pronoun used in statements and questions.

examples.trans: Do you need anything else from the kitchen?

examples.text: Hay algo dentro de la caja.
examples.trans: There is something inside the box.

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!
The weather is very nice today.
